en.title: Child Custody: What Should Parents Know?
en.directAnswer: Child custody is about who cares for a child in daily life. Guardianship concerns legal authority and can involve different questions. A court can consider the child’s welfare and the specific family facts. Do not rely on a simple internet rule that one parent always wins at a certain age.

atAGlance.whoFor: A parent wants a basic guide to custody and guardianship.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Family Courts Act, 2023; Guardians and Wards law; applicable personal law.
atAGlance.mainRule: Custody and guardianship should be explained separately. Existing court orders must be followed until changed by lawful process.
atAGlance.updateStatus: High-risk family-law page. Legal reviewer should verify current guardianship law citations before publication.

en.lawMeaning: Custody and guardianship should be explained separately. Existing court orders must be followed until changed by lawful process. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Keep school, medical and care records.
Do not hide the child or breach a court order.
Use the family-court/guardianship process when necessary.
evidence: Birth record; school records; medical records; care history; housing information; communications; existing court order.
en.simpleExample: Two parents separate and both say, “The child belongs to me.” The legal question is not ownership of a child. The court process focuses on lawful custody/guardianship and the child’s welfare.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Using the child as pressure.
Common mistakes: relying on fixed-age myths.
Common mistakes: taking a child abroad without checking legal restrictions..
